name: Dingolay
description: A star 158 parsecs away, 4.8 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 54158: radius 4.761 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 12.8 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.139) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 54158: effective temperature 5007 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.028)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 54158: distance 157.978 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.13), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 158 parsecs away, 4.8 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 13 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,007 K, so 4.761 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 54158: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 96063
quotes.card: HD 96063 is a 8th-magnitude red-giant branch star located about 454 light-years (139 pc) away in the constellation of Leo.
quotes.introduction: It is orbited by one confirmed exoplanet, HD 96063 b, a gas giant slightly larger and more massive than Jupiter.
